If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test is `testEqualsCS1`, which tests the `StringUtils.equals(CharSequence cs1, CharSequence cs2)` method with various `CharSequence` instances, including `StringBuilder`. The test fails when the method throws a String Index Out of Bounds Exception.

Looking at the `StringUtils.equals` method implementation, it first handles trivial cases (same reference, nulls, both strings). If both inputs are not strings but CharSequences (such as StringBuilder), it falls back to calling `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches`, passing the two CharSequences and the maximum length of the two sequences as the length to compare.

In the `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches` method, it attempts to compare `length` characters starting at specific offsets for both sequences. It does so by looping `length` times and calling `charAt` on each CharSequence at the current index values, incrementing after each character.

The critical problem is that the `length` argument given to `regionMatches` is `Math.max(cs1.length(), cs2.length())`, i.e., the longer length of the two sequences. When the sequences have different lengths, the loop in `regionMatches` tries to access characters beyond the shorter sequence's length, causing `charAt` to throw a String Index Out Of Bounds Exception.

The `regionMatches` method expects the `length` parameter to be the length of the common region to compare in both CharSequences, but `StringUtils.equals` mistakenly passes the length of the longer sequence, even if the other sequence is shorter. This mismatch leads to the out-of-bounds access.

In summary, the bug is caused by `StringUtils.equals` passing an incorrect length argument (`Math.max` length) to `CharSequenceUtils.regionMatches` when the two CharSequences have different lengths, which leads to an index out-of-bounds exception during character access.

This analysis is consistent with the current bug report's description that the method can fail with a String Index Out of Bounds error when sequences have different lengths.

Recent bug reports do not add relevant insight here since they address unrelated problems.

Correcting the call in `StringUtils.equals` to pass the minimum length of the two sequences instead of the maximum would avoid this error and fix the bug.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
